clinician.final_diagnosis: Simultaneous spontaneous bilateral ganglia hemorrhage secondary to uncontrolled hypertension
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old man with a history of poorly controlled hypertension and poor medication compliance presented to the emergency department with a 2-day history of severe headache, worsening confusion, and right-sided weakness. On initial examination, he was stuporous with GCS 8/15, right-sided weakness (0/5 motor strength), and mixed aphasia with preserved repetition. Pupils were symmetrically equal and reactive. Non-contrast CT head on admission revealed bilateral basal ganglia hemorrhage (5×3 cm left, 3×1 cm right). Presenting blood pressure was 220/120 mmHg. Laboratory studies including coagulation markers, CBC, and biochemistry were all normal, ruling out coagulopathy. The patient was admitted to the ICU and managed conservatively with antihypertensive medications and mannitol for 5 days. His GCS improved from 8 to 11 by hospital day 2, and he was transferred to the neurology ward on day 5.
